1	# Rules: Project Landing Page
2	
3	- **R-v7q.** A project's Needs you lists the same things Home does, for that project alone, newest first, and isn't shown when nothing needs the person there.
4	  *shown-on: /f/:project @ typical*
5	- **R-2hx.** A design with a branch is listed under In progress and not under Designs; once its branch is finished, it's listed under Designs again.
6	  *shown-on: /f/:project @ typical*
7	- **R-k4n.** Pushing a branch is always asked first, saying which branch goes to which remote, and nothing is pushed until the person says yes.
8	  *shown-on: /f/:project/branches/:branch/publish @ typical*
9	- **R-8dz.** The page's work and its app follow what happens elsewhere without a reload: a turn, a build, a push or a merge changes them as it happens, and they're read again every five minutes for what Prelude can't see, such as a pull request merged on the Git server.
10	- **R-wm3.** New design offers the design system, the app shell and the architecture as kinds only until the project has one of each.
11	  *shown-on: /f/:project/designs/new @ new-project*
12	- **R-r6b.** A design under Designs says it's ready to build when it has approved pages not yet built, and only once the project's app exists. A design that changed since it was approved isn't ready: it says it changed, until it's approved again.
13	  *shown-on: /f/:project @ typical*
14	- **R-h2w.** Once the app is built, it can be run from the project's own folder with a command and address of its own, never the design host's, and the Run button always shows the command it runs, so clicking it is the approval.
15	  *shown-on: /f/:project @ typical*
16	- **R-p7c.** Building or connecting the app sets how it runs from here, so a newly built app can be run without setting anything; a command changed on this page applies on this computer only.
17	  *shown-on: /f/:project @ typical*

text:
1	# Prelude architecture
2	
3	Prelude is a tool for designing and then building an app with an agent: you pick a project, chat with the Claude Code CLI, and watch the design appear beside the chat. It runs as one Node server (plain `node:http`, views in Eta, Koda in the page) on localhost:4200, optionally inside a Tauri desktop window. Everything it produces is files in the project's `prelude/` folder, each design worked on in its own git branch and worktree. Agent-written views render in a sandboxed child process, and each design is served on its own preview origin.
4	
5	## Layers
6	
7	1. Windows
8	2. Entry points
9	3. Pages
10	4. Agent and live state
11	5. Designs and hosting
12	6. Project files
13	7. Shared helpers
14	8. Outside
15	
16	## Principles
17	
18	- **The folder is the database.** Everything Prelude makes is a file under the project's `prelude/`, committed with the code; `~/.prelude/` holds only machine-local conveniences, so nothing is lost if it's deleted.
19	- **The server is the single source of truth for live state.** Every window (chat, pop-out, browser tab) renders from the server and re-renders on its SSE events, so no window holds state another needs.
20	- **Agent-written code never runs in the server's process.** A design's views render in a sandboxed renderer, and a host that runs them unsandboxed starts only once the person approves it.
21	- **The agent works with ordinary file tools, fenced to what it may touch.** It reads the project and the folders added as references, writes only where its mode allows, and deletes by writing a file empty.
22	- **A design's memory is its files, not a conversation.** Each session starts from NOTES.md, the views and states, so sessions on different machines and branches pick up where the work stands.
23	- **Committed files must merge cleanly.** Session folders and decision ids are random, transcripts are append-only, and there's no shared index that every session rewrites.

1	# Project Landing Page - notes
2	
3	A project's own page (`/f/<id>`), a redesign of `server/views/_folder.eta` (with
4	`_branch.eta`), whose model is built in `server/main.js` (`view()` in the
5	`/f/:id` handler). Home (prelude/landing-page) gathers what needs the person
6	across projects and links here; this page holds the project's whole picture.
7	
8	Pages: `/f/:project` (Project), `/f/:project/designs/new` (New design, modal),
9	`/f/:project/branches/:branch/publish` (Push a branch, modal),
10	`/f/:project/cleanup` (Clean up, modal), `/f/:project/branches/:branch/discard`
11	(Discard a branch, modal), `/f/:project/app/koda` (Upgrade Koda, modal).
12	Fragments: `/f/:project/work`, `/f/:project/app`. States: typical
13	(spark-lending), new project, app being built, update clashed (with the app
14	on the shell's branch and a failed push), long names (an existing app to
15	connect, no remote), large project (a hundred features), Koda behind, Koda
16	upgrading, Koda to install. Also `/f/:project/app/koda/install` (modal).
17	
18	## Decisions (the person asked for all eleven, 2026-10-18)
19	
20	1. **On the design system**, not ds/v1 + `prelude.css`, like Home.
21	2. **Work beside setup**: a `.split` in a `.center.wide`. Main: Needs you, In
22	   progress, Designs. Side: The app, What the agent can read. Added
23	   `.center.wide` / `--measure-wide` to the design system (46rem can't hold a
24	   split).
25	3. **New design is a modal**, opened by the header's "New design…", the page's
26	   one primary action. A refused title comes back into the fields alone
27	   (`_new-design-fields`); made, the modal closes and the page refreshes (the
28	   real app opens the new design's page).
29	4. **One primary per view**: Merge, Push, Start the app build are plain buttons.
30	5. **A branch's state as pills**: check, building / build stopped, behind main,

server\views\build\session.eta:57: <% if (it.live) { %>
<% } %> server\views\host\layout.eta:28:<% if (it.layout?.live) { %>
<% } %> server\views\_regions.eta:33:<% if (it.layout?.live) { %>
<% } %> server\views\_session.eta:39: <% if (it.live) { %>
<% } %>

I didn't change any files. All six events were already sent from the code where each change happens, over the app's live channel. The project page's regions already reload on them.

| Event | Where it's sent | What reloads |
|---|---|---|
| `needs-changed` (the agent asks something on Loan offers) | A question is a turn ending. When a turn ends, `server/turns.js:347` tells `server/main.js:116`, which calls `tell(app, { needs: true, projects: true })` in `server/home.js:325`. | The work region (`server/views/projects/page.eta:59`) |
| `projects-changed` (Rate lock's page renders again and its build carries on) | The same turn-end call, sent after the check that renders the pages again. When the build carries on, the next turn starting sends it too (`server/turns.js:257`). | The work, Designs and app regions |
| `app-changed` from `app-running` / `app-failed` | `server/runs.js:177-179` once the app answers at its address. For a failure, `server/runs.js:152-158` (it exits before answering) or `:168-171` (nothing answers within three minutes). Both go through `createRuns({ onChange })` at `server/main.js:124`. | The app card (`server/views/projects/page.eta:93`) |
| `app-changed` from `koda-installed` / `koda-install-failed` | `server/installs.js:85-91` when an install ends either way, through `createInstalls({ onChange })` at `server/main.js:126`. | The app card |

The channel itself was already there: `tell()` sends to the app's channel, and the layout opens it with `ko-connect="<%= it.layout.live %>"` (`server/views/_regions.eta:33`). It sends the named event only; any markup comes from the region reloading.

RULES.md has no *proposed* lines, so I left it alone. Nothing in the architecture changes, so I didn't propose a decision.

Two things are worth checking before you approve:
- **An install in the upgrade's own branch also sends `app-changed`.** That's harmless, because the card just reads its state again.
- **A question shows up when the turn ends, not while it's still going.** That's when a question is counted as needing you, the same as on Home.
